title: One fret, one half step
summary: Each fret is one half step higher than the one before it.

steps.title: A step up for every fret
steps.body:
Moving up one fret raises the note by the smallest step in music, a **half step**. Two frets make two half steps. The open string counts as fret 0.

**Why it matters:** This one rule lets you find every note on the neck. Count the frets from an open string and you know the note.

steps.title: Counting from the open string
steps.body:
On the A string, the open string is A. Fret 1 is the next sound up, fret 2 is the one after that, and so on. Count every fret as one small move; do not skip a fret just because you do not know its name yet.

**Why it matters:** You can measure a move by counting frets without knowing any piano keys. The later notes lessons will give each sound its name.

steps.title: The first frets of the A string
steps.body: Play the open A string, then each of the next four frets, one after the other.

steps.title: Walk up a string
steps.body: Start on any open string and play each fret in turn up to fret 5. Listen to the pitch climb in small steps.
